criteria.criterion: After every Copilot work session the driver reads the session's JSON Lines; a call that ran is a `tool.execution_start` whose `tool.execution_complete` of the same `data.toolCallId` does not carry `data.error.code` `denied`, or that has no completion.
criteria.evidence: internal/driver/fencecheck.go bypassedCalls pairs start/complete by toolCallId; fencecheck_test.go covers no-completion, denied and completed calls

criteria.criterion: Each call that ran is judged by `fence.New(phase, root, home)` and `Decide` — the hook's own judge — with tool, path and command read from `data.toolName` and `data.arguments` exactly as `parseHookPayload` reads `toolName` and `toolArgs` (an object, or a JSON string holding one; `path`; a skill's `skill` or `name`; apply_patch's `input`, `patch` or `command`), and with the hook's rule first: a `bash` or `powershell` call with an empty command is denied with `the \u003ctool\u003e call has no command the hook can read`. Violation: a second argument parser that can diverge from the hook's, or any judge or rule list other than the hook's.
criteria.evidence: internal/cli/fence.go CallJudge reuses parseHookPayload and the extracted decideCall (empty-command rule then j.Decide) that the hook itself now calls; no second parser

criteria.criterion: The driver does not import `internal/fence` (which imports `internal/driver`); the judge reaches the driver another way (for example as a function the CLI hands it). The check is the phases', not `Runner.Run`'s: `tools/agent-eval` and its tests are unchanged.
criteria.evidence: driver.CallJudge func type, Iterator.Judge set in internal/cli/run.go; tools/agent-eval untouched in git status

criteria.criterion: With one or more denied, stderr has one line per denied call, `vloop: \u003ctool\u003e \u003cwhat\u003e — \u003cthe judge's reason\u003e`, `\u003cwhat\u003e` the call's path, else the first line of its command cut to 200 runes with `…` added when cut, else nothing (`vloop: \u003ctool\u003e — \u003creason\u003e`); then the run halts with exit 9 and `FENCE BYPASSED work — the session ran \u003cn\u003e call(s) its fence denies; nothing from it was used`. Every line is masked (`$HOME` as `~`) and written to the run log too, as `REFS MOVED`'s warnings are.
criteria.evidence: iterate.go fenceBypassed uses it.warn (masks, logs, prints) then haltGit; formats covered by TestBypassedCalls and TestRunFenceBackstopBypassed

criteria.criterion: The check runs as soon as the work session ends, whatever its exit, before the phase's own checks (so before REFS MOVED); the phase still makes its restores of the driver's inputs before exiting 9; the halt comes before the proposal is used or anything is committed, and the work tree is otherwise left as the session left it. With no call denied nothing changes and nothing is printed. A Claude session's handling is unchanged (violation: any change to how a Claude session is run, parsed or halted).
criteria.evidence: iterate.go workSession: fenceBypassed after restoreInputs, before gitChanged/gitRefsMoved/readReport; Run gates the judge on the Copilot agent

criteria.criterion: Committed tests: the worked example's first three lines as one `cmd/vloop` test each (a work session's bash `git commit -m x` completed without error -> the two stderr lines, exit 9, no new commit; the same call completed `denied` -> the iteration goes on; a bash `ls` only -> the iteration goes on), with the harness's stub `copilot` gaining, in test code, the prompts of every phase (`/vloop:<phase>` with or without an argument) and the tool events a test's copilot-script.sh asks for; and tests of the reading of fixture JSON Lines (a call with no completion, a denied completion, the path / first-line / 200-rune / nothing forms of `<what>`, the empty-command rule). `TestRunHarnessCopilot`'s refusal of `/vloop:work T1` changes only to pin a prompt the stub still refuses; no other existing test changes.
criteria.evidence: The three cmd/vloop tests and the 200-rune/path/nothing forms exist, but no committed test covers the empty-command rule (grep finds no test referencing decideCall, CallJudge or 'has no command the hook can read'); TestBypassedCalls uses a fake judge, so the real CallJudge reading is untested. The first-line (multi-line) form is only checked together with the 200-rune cut.

findings.summary: No committed test exercises the empty-command rule or the real CallJudge (string toolArgs, hook-parser reading), which the acceptance lists explicitly

notes: Implementation otherwise matches the brief. Add a test of CallJudge in internal/cli (empty bash/powershell command denied with the hook's message; toolArgs as a JSON string).
